prompt_en: A candid photograph of an adult woman in her mid-twenties making a private late-night confession in her own bedroom. Seen from the camera as the person receiving her confession, she sits securely on the mattress, wearing a loose cotton pajama shirt and soft lounge trousers, with slightly tousled hair. She offers her handwritten love letter toward the lens, holding the sheet by its two side edges with both hands, elbows bent close to her torso. The paper sits just below her chin and tilts toward the camera; her face remains visible just above the letter. Written in large, legible, slightly uneven dark-ink handwriting is the exact sentence "Will you be my boyfriend?" with a tiny hand-drawn heart underneath. The written question now faces the recipient in the foreground. Her gaze stays on the recipient while she waits for an answer; the corners of her lips lift into a small, hopeful smile. Rumpled bedding, a softly glowing bedside lamp and a black window establish a quiet bedroom after midnight. An early-2000s compact CCD-camera snapshot with direct on-camera flash: bright facial highlights, crisp shadows behind her, luminous paper with visible ink, warm room light receding into deep shadows, fine digital noise and slightly faded colors. Pale ivory bedding and a muted rose pillow gently frame the dark-ink message. A vertical 3:4 composition places her face in the upper third and the letter across the middle, keeping the bedside lamp and a margin of bedding visible. The photograph feels close, personal and unpolished, preserving the vulnerable pause between handing over the letter and hearing a reply.
negative_en: excessive HDR, 3D render look, unrealistic hands, broken facial features, cartoon style, warped walls, low resolution, illustration look
